title: Below-level factorization of singleton projection through semilinear reduction
statement: Let C be a category with independent object and morphism universes c,v, J a Grothendieck topology, and C essentially small in max(c,v,r). Let B_n be commutative ring sheaves with maps tau_n : B_(n+1) to B_n, with coefficient universe max(c,v,r). Use the actual sequence-site module systems, ordinary unbounded derived category DS, derived evaluations e_n, and derived reductions of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Fix closed tensor structures, K-flat models, tensorEvaluation isomorphisms and TensorComparisonModel data normalized by ordinaryEvaluationTensor as in [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus]. For any derived system M, indices q at most n, normalized scalar data A for B_n to B_q, an adjunction adj : L left adjoint to e_n, and P in D(B_n), there is an isomorphism alpha : e_q L(P tensor M_n) to e_q(LP) tensor A.T(M_n). If f : L(P tensor M_n) to LP tensor M is the inverse adjunction transpose of (unit_P tensor id_M_n) followed by tensorEvaluation_n inverse, then e_q(f) followed by tensorEvaluation_q equals alpha followed by tensor(id,reduction_A(M,n,q)). There is no cartesianness assumption and no claim that reduction or f is invertible. The exact object and morphism formulas, including all universes, are the Lean statement in lean.statement.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p.21; Proposition 4.17(a) and its proof, printed pp.25-26. The unit-defined projection argument is step 2 of lem-coef-semilinear-cartesian-hom-evaluation; the extension from constant quotient rings to arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings is the same local tensor computation.

proof.text: Choose normalized scalar data for all coefficient maps and scalar tensor comparisons using semilinearScalarTensor. Package the given tensor models and these comparisons in SystemTensorReductionModels, without choosing any internal-Hom comparison. The tensor-reduction core proves the actual reduction tensor identity.

Reduction is a natural transformation delta from e_n followed by scalar extension to e_q. Compose scalar extension of the unit of L with delta to form kappa from scalar extension to L followed by e_q. The below-level singleton mate theorem makes every kappa component invertible. Define alpha as kappa inverse on P tensor M_n, then scalar tensor comparison, then tensor(kappa_P,id).

For f the inverse adjunction transpose in the statement, unit followed by e_n(f) equals tensor(unit,id) followed by inverse evaluation comparison. Naturality of delta, tensor reduction, and naturality of scalar tensor comparison identify the two sides after precomposition by kappa; cancel it. The private proved factorization_of_tensor_reduction writes this calculation. Finally the unique unit-compatible isomorphism from the chosen scalar adjunction to the supplied A identifies reductions and transports alpha.

lean.statement:
theorem semilinearProjectionBelowFactorization
    (closed : Closed.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ))
    (models : Models.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) closed)
    (level : ∀ n : ℕ, Closed.{c, v, r} J (B n))
    (levelModels : ∀ n : ℕ, Models.{c, v, r} J (B n) (level n))
    (tensorEvaluation : ∀ n : ℕ,
      closed.tensor ⋙ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n ≅
        ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).prod
          (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)) ⋙ (level n).tensor)
    (tensorModel : ∀ n : ℕ,
      TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J) J
        (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (B n)
        (evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n) closed (level n) models
        (levelModels n) (tensorEvaluation n))
    (ordinary : ∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ),
      (tensorModel n).ordinary M N = ordinaryEvaluationTensor.{c, v, r} J B τ n M N)
    (M : DS.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (n q : ℕ) (h : q ≤ n)
    (A : ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r}
      (coefficientMap.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ h))
    (L : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n) ⥤ DS.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ)
    (adj : L ⊣ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)
    (P : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n)) :
    ∃ α : (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ q).obj
        (L.obj ((level n).tensor.obj (P, (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj M))) ≅
      (level q).tensor.obj
        ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ q).obj (L.obj P),
          A.T.obj ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj M)),
      (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ q).map
          ((adj.homEquiv _ _).symm
            ((level n).tensor.map
                (Prod.mkHom (adj.unit.app P)
                  (𝟙 ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj M))) ≫
              (tensorEvaluation n).inv.app (L.obj P, M))) ≫
        (tensorEvaluation q).hom.app (L.obj P, M) =
      α.hom ≫ (level q).tensor.map
        (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ q).obj (L.obj P)))
          (reduction.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ h A M))
